title: Unit 7 · Food and restaurants
description: Food and drink, meals, ordering politely, quantities, preferences, and restaurant language.
source: Original exercises aligned to the Aula Internacional Plus 1 Unit 7 syllabus; no textbook exercise text copied.

cards.translation: I need bread for the sandwich.
cards.note: El pan is bread.
De queso means with a cheese filling.

cards.translation: The sandwich contains ham and tomato.
cards.note: El tomate is tomato.

cards.translation: Today we are eating chicken with rice.
cards.note: El pollo is chicken.

cards.prompt: No como carne, pero sí como ___.
cards.translation: I don't eat meat, but I do eat fish.
cards.note: El pescado is fish as food.
El arroz is rice.
Patatas is common in Spain; papas is common in much of Latin America.

cards.translation: It is important to eat plenty of vegetables.
cards.note: Las verduras are vegetables.
La fruta is fruit as a food category.
Una manzana is an apple.
Zumo de naranja means orange juice.
Agua is feminine but uses el in the singular: el agua.

cards.translation: I want a coffee with milk.
cards.note: Café con leche is coffee with milk.

cards.translation: In the afternoon I drink tea.
cards.note: Té with an accent means tea.

cards.prompt: El ___ es la primera comida del día.
cards.translation: Breakfast is the first meal of the day.
cards.note: El desayuno is breakfast.

cards.prompt: La ___ principal suele ser al mediodía.
cards.translation: The main meal is usually at midday.
cards.note: In Spain, la comida often means the midday meal.

cards.prompt: La ___ es la comida de la noche.
cards.note: La cena is dinner.

cards.translation: For dessert I want ice cream.
cards.note: De postre means for dessert.

cards.translation: Could you bring us the menu, please?
cards.note: La carta is the restaurant menu.

cards.translation: I would like the soup, please.
cards.note: Querer changes e to ie: quiero.
Por favor makes the order polite.

cards.translation: What would you like to have?
cards.note: Desear is a polite way to ask what someone wants.

cards.translation: For my first course, I will have a salad.
cards.note: De primero introduces the first course.

cards.translation: For my main course, I want fish.
cards.note: De segundo introduces the second or main course.
La cuenta is the bill.
El servicio is service.
Rica agrees with the feminine noun sopa.
Use gusta with the singular noun pescado.
Use encantan with a plural noun.
Preferir changes e to ie: prefiero.
Sin means without.
Con hielo means with ice.

cards.translation: I want a chocolate ice cream.
cards.note: De introduces the flavor.
Una taza de is a cup of.
Un vaso de is a glass of.
Una botella de is a bottle of.
Un kilo de is a kilogram of.

cards.prompt: La sopa necesita un poco de ___.
cards.translation: The soup needs a little salt.
cards.note: Un poco de means a little of.

cards.translation: I drink a lot of water.
cards.note: Mucha agrees with the feminine noun agua despite el agua in the singular.

cards.translation: I don't eat meat; I am vegetarian.
cards.note: The ending agrees with the speaker.
Use alérgico a for allergic to.

cards.translation: How do you take your coffee?
cards.note: Tomar is used for having food or drink.
